title: Correlations computed from officially sourced numbers, with n published
method: Pearson r; 95% interval by Fisher z (stated as a floor on width because games inside a week are not fully independent); two-sided permutation p with 10000 shuffles and seed 20261117.
policy: a blank r always carries its reason in the same row; no value is estimated

rows.definition: (home - away) points versus (home + away) points, one pair per game
rows.note: the size of the relationship that makes a same-game parlay of side and total dependent. It is measured here so it never has to be assumed.

rows.definition: the pre-kickoff model total versus the total actually scored, walk-forward weeks only
rows.note: a high value is necessary but not sufficient for a useful totals model; it is not a market test.

rows.definition: the pre-kickoff model margin (home perspective) versus the actual margin
rows.note: this is the side model's own skill, measured on outcomes it never saw.

rows.pair: rest differential (home - away, days) ~ home margin
rows.definition: rest days computed from the official dates of consecutive fixtures (a schedule fact, not an estimate), versus the game margin
rows.note: rest is derived from published dates only. The first appearance of each club is dropped because its prior game is outside the corpus.

rows.definition: whether playing at a neutral site changes the home margin
rows.blank_reason: only 2 corpus games are venue-verified as neutral from the official pages this session read (the Week-9 Madrid and Week-10 Munich fixtures). The inherited feed flags more, but a peer flag is not a verification, so those are carried separately in the corpus and are not used here. A correlation on n=2 is undefined, so the row is blank.
